**Service Name: Netflix Terms of Use**

These terms outline the agreement between you and Netflix when using their services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all Netflix products and services, and cover your relationship with the company.
* **Content and License:** You grant Netflix permission to use content you submit, subject to your settings and applicable law. This means they can use data from you to improve their services, but they must follow your settings and any laws that apply.
* **Privacy:** Your personal data is governed by Netflix's published Privacy Policy, which explains what data is collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** In case of a dispute, you and Netflix will go to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). You can opt out of this within 30 days of creating a new account.
* **Termination:** Either you or Netflix can terminate the agreement at any time, subject to conditions outlined in the live document (which you can access at the specified URL).
* **Contact:** If you have questions about these terms, you can contact Netflix at the address listed on their website.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* **Dispute Resolution:** The requirement for binding arbitration with a class-action waiver (meaning you can't join a group lawsuit) may limit your ability to seek damages or justice if something goes wrong with your Netflix account. This can only be opted out of within 30 days of creating a new account.
* **Termination:** While either party can terminate the agreement, it's not clear under what specific conditions this can happen. Be aware that this could leave you without access to your Netflix account or account data without notice.

Overall, these terms require you to agree to binding arbitration and class-action waivers, and give Netflix broad permission to use your content for their own purposes. Be sure to read through the full document to understand your rights and responsibilities with Netflix.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NETFLIX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Netflix and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected the household sharing/'extra member' policy: paid sharing requires the primary household plus paid additional members, added clearer language on what constitutes a 'Netflix Household', and updated billing/cancellation provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Netflix to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse .

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DISNEY+ SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Disney+ and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones: streaming titles may now show ads even on 'no ads'/'ad free' tiers, expanded arbitration with mass-arbitration procedures following Disney's earlier 2024 Wrongful-Death-case controversy, and updated content-availability language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Disney+ to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement .

**Service Name:** PayPal User Agreement

These updated Terms of Service, effective 2024, outline the rules and guidelines for using PayPal's products and services. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all PayPal products and services listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** PayPal can use your user-submitted content to improve and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. However, this clause might be vague, and the term "applicable law" could leave room for different interpretations.
* **Privacy:** The terms cross-reference PayPal's published Privacy Policy, which outlines the types of personal data collected and how it's processed. This suggests that PayPal's data collection practices are governed by a separate policy, which may be subject to change.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration with class-action waivers, meaning you may not be able to join a class-action lawsuit. This provision also has a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. Binding arbitration can be a private process that limits your recourse, but it's a common practice in online contracts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to conditions described in the live document. This means PayPal can end your account without warning if you don't meet their requirements or terms.

**Clauses that may be harmful to users:**

* **Binding arbitration and class-action waivers** may limit users' ability to seek collective redress in cases of widespread issues or system failures.
* **PayPal's ability to use user content** might be broad, which could raise concerns about data ownership and control.

**Recommendation:**

* Review PayPal's Privacy Policy to understand what types of data they collect and how it's processed.
* If you're not comfortable with binding arbitration, create a new account or contact PayPal's customer support for alternative dispute resolution.
* Review the **Termination** clause to understand when PayPal can end your account.

Keep in mind that these clauses are standard in many online contracts, but it's essential to understand your rights and responsibilities as a PayPal user.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PAYPAL USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Multiple 2024 updates: revised seller-protection criteria, added new fee schedules for cross-border transactions, expanded the dispute resolution / chargeback flow, and clarified handling of cryptocurrency holdings. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . The previous version is available at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

response:
**Service:** eBay User Agreement

**Summary:** The eBay User Agreement is a set of rules governing your relationship with eBay. These terms outline how you and eBay interact, what happens with your submitted content, and how to resolve disputes.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to services and products offered by eBay, as listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** eBay uses your submitted content to improve and train their AI and machine learning (AI/ML) systems, if you don't object and in accordance with applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** eBay's published Privacy Policy explains how it collects and processes your personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes will be resolved through private binding arbitration, which means you give up the right to a court trial and must agree to a private dispute process (binding arbitration). You have a 30-day window to opt-out when you create a new account, but you must do it within that timeframe.
* **Termination:** Either you or eBay can end the agreement under certain conditions as described in the document.
* **Contact:** You can find information on these terms and the company's general contact information on their published legal contact page.

**Clauses that May be Harmful to the User:**

* **Binding Arbitration:** As mentioned earlier, this means giving up the right to a court trial and using a private dispute process instead. This can be limiting for users seeking broader protections and more control over their cases.
* **Class-Action Waivers:** This means you cannot join a group lawsuit against eBay, potentially limiting your ability to seek collective compensation.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EBAY USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with eBay and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised payments-on-eBay structure for managed payments, added more detailed AI/automated-decision sections, expanded permitted-use language for listing data, and updated arbitration / opt-out procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by eBay to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 .

**Service Name:** Amazon Conditions of Use (effective 2024)

**Summary:** These Terms of Service outline how you (the user) interact with Amazon and govern the products and services provided by the company. The key provisions are:

* **Scope**: These terms apply to any product or service listed on Amazon's official terms page.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content (e.g., reviews, photos), Amazon uses it to improve and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Your personal data is subject to Amazon's Privacy Policy, which explains how data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes are resolved through binding arbitration, which means a private judge instead of a court. However, you can opt out of this within 30 days of creating a new account.
* **Termination**: Either Amazon or you can terminate this agreement as outlined in the live document.
* **Contact**: Questions about these terms can be directed to Amazon's published contact information.

**Flags of concern for the user:**

* **Binding arbitration**: This means you waive your right to a courtroom trial and instead will resolve disputes privately with a designated judge. Note that you can opt out within 30 days, but it's a time-limited opportunity.
* **Class-action waivers**: By using Amazon's services, you might give up the right to join class-action lawsuits against Amazon.
* **Use of user-submitted content**: While Amazon uses content to improve its services, it's essential to be aware of how your contributions (e.g., reviews, photos) are used and shared.
* **Termination**: Be aware that either party can terminate this agreement, which might impact your access to Amazon services.

**Additional information:** To understand your data collection and processing, please review Amazon's Privacy Policy separately. If you have specific questions or concerns, review Amazon's contact information at the provided URL.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — AMAZON CONDITIONS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Amazon and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: May 2024 update revised disputes/arbitration to explicitly permit small-claims-court actions, updated language about Amazon services covered, and added clearer references to AI features (Alexa, Rufus) and how generated content interacts with the user agreement.

response:
The service is called Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions. To summarize, the Terms of Service outline Apple's rules for using their digital media services, which include products like Apple Music, iCloud, and the App Store.

Here are the key provisions:

**Scope**: These terms apply to your relationship with Apple and control how you use their services.

**Content and License**: Apple can use your submitted content, like data or media, to improve their AI/ML systems, but only if you've allowed it in your settings or if it's required by the law.

**Privacy**: Apple's Privacy Policy explains how they collect and process your personal data, but you should read that policy specifically for details.

**Dispute Resolution**: If a dispute arises, Apple wants to resolve it through private arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. However, Steam (Valve) is not required to use this method. Note that class-action lawsuits are not an option in these arbitration proceedings.

One potential concern is the dispute resolution clause, which may limit your ability to take action in court or join a class-action lawsuit if you have a problem with Apple.

Here are the other key provisions:

- You can terminate the agreement, but the Terms and Conditions require specific conditions.
- Apple can also terminate the agreement under certain conditions.
- If you have questions about these Terms of Service, you can contact Apple through their published contact information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — APPLE MEDIA SERVICES TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features, clarified content-license scope across services (iCloud, Apple Music, App Store), and revised Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html .

The service name is iCloud. Here's a plain-language summary of the key provisions:

**Overview**

These terms govern your relationship with Apple and outline the rules for using their iCloud services.

**Key Provisions**

* **Content Use**: When you upload content to iCloud, Apple may use it to improve their products, services, or AI/ML systems, but will follow your settings and applicable law.
* **Data Sharing**: Your content may be accessed by Apple if necessary for legal or safety reasons.
* **Arbitration**: If a dispute arises, you'll need to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers, unless you opt out within 30 days of creating your account.
* **Termination**: Either you or Apple can end the agreement at any time, but you should review the live document for terms.
* **Contact**: For questions, see Apple's published contact information.

**Harmful Clauses Flagged**

* While not explicitly stated, there's no clear guarantee about user data protection, raising concerns about data handling and storage practices.
* The binding arbitration provision may limit users' ability to seek redress in court, potentially making disputes more difficult to resolve.
* The clause allowing Apple to access users' content for legal or safety reasons doesn't provide specific information about what these reasons entail, which may raise data protection concerns.

**Other Concerns**

* There's a notice about the 30-day opt-out window for arbitration, but no clear instructions on how to do so.
* Previous versions of the Terms of Service are not available, making it difficult to assess changes and any implications for users who continued to use the service.

Keep in mind that these are the main concerns and inferences drawn from the provided text. Users should consider their individual circumstances and concerns when using the service.

Note that this is not a legal analysis but rather a summary of the terms provided.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ICLOUD TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Advanced Data Protection (end-to-end encryption) language, references to Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, and revised provisions about how stored content may be accessed by Apple for legal/safety reasons.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html .

**Service Name:** Snap Terms of Service, also referred to as Snapchat terms.

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope**: These terms apply to your relationship with Snap and its services, including products and services listed on the company's official terms page.
2. **Content and License**: Snap can use your submitted content to operate and improve its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
3. **Privacy**: The terms reference the company's separate Privacy Policy, which explains the personal data collected and how it's processed.
4. **Dispute Resolution**: Most provisions require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, except for new accounts which have a 30-day opt-out window. This means that any disputes are resolved privately, and you can't join a class-action lawsuit.
5. **Termination**: Either you or Snap can end the agreement under certain conditions, as described in the live document.

**Concerns and Red Flags:**

* **Arbitration clauses**: The requirement for binding arbitration with class-action waivers may limit your ability to join a class-action lawsuit. This could be a concern if you're a group of users affected by a similar issue. (Binding arbitration is a private dispute process instead of going to court.)
* **No prior versions available**: As this is the latest version, we're not aware of any prior terms to compare. However, this might indicate that the company has updated its terms significantly since 2024.
* **Data usage and sharing**: The terms mention that Snap can use your submitted content to improve its AI/ML systems. This may raise concerns about how your data is used, especially with the introduction of new AI features like My AI.

It's essential to be aware of these provisions and understand how they might impact your user experience and data protection. If you're unsure about any aspect, it's a good idea to review the terms thoroughly or direct specific questions to Snap's customer support or legal team.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SNAP TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Snap (Snapchat) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective April 7, 2025: added new sections on My AI and other generative-AI features, expanded the user-content license for Live/Local/crowd-sourced services, clarified data-sharing with parents (for under-18 users via Family Center), and updated arbitration pre-dispute notice procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Snap (Snapchat) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.snap.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.snap.com/terms .

**Key Provisions:**

* *Scope*: These terms govern your relationship with Pinterest and cover the products and services offered on Pinterest's official terms page.
* *Content and License*: When you submit content to Pinterest, you grant the company permission to use it to operate, improve, and train AI/ML systems (subject to your settings and applicable law).

* *Dispute Resolution*: Users may be required to participate in binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. This means you may not be able to join a class-action lawsuit against Pinterest.
* *Termination*: Either you or Pinterest may terminate the agreement under certain conditions.
* *Contact*: If you have questions or concerns about these terms, see Pinterest's published legal contact information.

**Provisions that may be Harmful to the User:**

* *Dispute Resolution*: Requiring binding arbitration with class-action waivers may limit your ability to take part in a class-action lawsuit against Pinterest.
* *Termination*: Pinterest may terminate the agreement without giving specific reasons (subject to the conditions described in the live document).

Keep in mind that these are the main points and do not cover every aspect of the Terms of Service. It's essential to review the actual document for specific details and conditions.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PINTEREST TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Pinterest and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added language permitting Pinterest to use public Pin content to train AI/ML models for recommendations and safety, clarified obligations for advertisers and merchants, and updated arbitration provisions. Pinterest publishes a public archive at policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Pinterest to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive .

The service is called Tumblr Terms of Service. Here's a plain-language summary of the key provisions:

**Service Overview**
Tumblr Terms of Service is the agreement between you (the user) and Tumblr, regarding your use of the service.

**Key Provisions**

* **Scope**: These terms apply to all Tumblr products and services.
* **Content and License**: You submit content to Tumblr, which may be used to improve and train AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: The company's Privacy Policy explains how personal data is collected and processed.
* **Binding Arbitration**: In the event of a dispute, most users must participate in private arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to conditions listed in the document.
* **Opt-out for AI Training**: You can control how your public content is used by opting out of public AI training in Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing.

**Flags of Concern**

* The requirement for binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) may limit your access to the courts.
* Some users may find the opt-out requirements for AI training and arbitration procedures restrictive or onerous.

**Recommendation**
Please read the full Terms of Service document for a complete understanding of the agreement.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TUMBLR TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Tumblr and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected Automattic's deal to share public Tumblr posts with AI partners (e.g. for training): added language confirming use of public content for AI training and added a user-facing opt-out (Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Tumblr to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service .

The service name is Dropbox Terms of Service. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope**: These Terms of Service apply to all Dropbox products and services as listed on Dropbox's official terms page.

**Key Provisions**:

* **Data Use**: Dropbox may use your uploaded content to operate, improve, and train its AI and machine learning (ML) systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. Specifically, your data isn't used to train third-party AI models without your consent.
* **Data Collection and Processing**: Dropbox collects and processes personal data, which is governed by a separate Privacy Policy. 
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most users are required to resolve disputes through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) under a class-action waiver. However, users have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. Note that Steam (Valve) is excluded from this mandatory arbitration.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under specific conditions, as outlined in the Terms.

**Flags of potential concern**:

* **Data Use**: While it's reassuring that your data isn't used to train third-party AI models without consent, it's still unclear how Dropbox uses your uploaded content to operate and improve its services. Users may want to review the Content and License section for more details.
* **Dispute Resolution**: The requirement for binding arbitration with a class-action waiver might limit your options for seeking justice if you encounter an issue with Dropbox's service. The 30-day opt-out window for new accounts is a positive step, but users should consider the trade-off.
* **Termination**: The specific conditions under which either party can terminate the agreement are not detailed here. Users may want to review the live document for further information.

Please note that the above analysis is based solely on the provided Terms of Service, which may have additional provisions or implications not captured here.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DROPBOX TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Dropbox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Late-2023/early-2024 update added Dropbox AI features (Dropbox Dash, AI search/summary). After user backlash, Dropbox amended language (Dec 2023 / 2024) to explicitly state customer data is not used to train third-party AI models without consent.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Dropbox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.dropbox.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230601000000*/https://www.dropbox.com/terms .

**Service Name:** Canva Terms of Use (TOS)

**Key Provisions:**

* The Canva TOS is a binding agreement between you (the user) and Canva, governing your use of their products and services.
* Canva reserves the right to change or terminate the service at any time, subject to certain conditions.
* **Generated Content:** If you use Canva's generative AI tools (Magic Studio), you own the output, but Canva retains certain platform rights and restrictions apply to using such content to train other AI models. Be aware that you're subject to new content-moderation and labeling requirements.
* **Content and License:** Canva uses your submitted content to operate and improve their AI/ML systems, following your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The TOS references Canva's published Privacy Policy, explaining what personal data is collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** You agree to binding arbitration, which is a private dispute process instead of court (although you can opt-out within 30 days of creating a new account). This means you won't have access to a traditional court system.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to conditions in the live document.

**Potential Concerns:**

* The use of binding arbitration may limit your access to a traditional court system and the ability to participate in class-action suits.
* The terms for generated content may restrict how you use AI-generated content, raising questions about ownership and control.
* The TOS does not explicitly provide for a clear way to resolve disputes outside of arbitration.

**Where to Seek Help:**

If you have questions or concerns about the Canva TOS, refer to the company's published legal contact information at the Canva website.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — CANVA TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Canva and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Canva's generative AI tools (Magic Studio): users own outputs subject to platform rights, restrictions on using Canva-generated content to train other AI models, and new content-moderation/labeling requirements.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Canva to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ .

The main service in question is called Notion Terms of Service. Here's a summary of what this agreement entails:

**Key Provisions:**

### Scope and Relationship

- These terms govern your relationship with Notion and apply to the company's products and services mentioned on their official terms page.

### Content and Use of Your Data

- When you submit content, Notion can use it for its own operations, improvement, and to train its AI and machine learning systems.
- The company might share aspects of this information for regulatory compliance or other essential purposes.

### Data Collection (Linked to Privacy Policy)

- The Notion Privacy Policy sets out how Notion collects and processes user data.

Red flags for users:
* The terms allow Notion to use your submitted content for its proprietary work.

### Dispute Resolution (Arbitration)

- Users must resolve disputes through binding arbitration, which is a private adjudication process instead of seeking a court settlement. This also comes with a class-action waiver, preventing users from joining a collective lawsuit.

* Users with new accounts may opt-out of the arbitration requirement within a 30-day window.

### Termination

- Both Notion and users can terminate their agreement subject to the conditions in the live document.

### Getting Help and Feedback

- If you have questions about these terms, you can find Notion's contact information at https://www.notion.com/terms.

The Terms of Service do not address the following topics:

* How you can request deletion of your data
* If third-party involvement may affect user recourse or liability

These statements and conditions aim to provide a clear and concise understanding of Notion Terms of Service without introducing or removing any additional content.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NOTION TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Notion and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Notion AI provisions (input/output ownership, no training of foundational models on customer data by default), updated subprocessor list, and clarified data-residency options for enterprise plans.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Notion to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.notion.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.notion.so/terms .

**Service Name: Figma Terms of Service**

The current version of the Figma Terms of Service governs the relationship between you (the user) and Figma. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope**: These terms apply to the products and services listed on Figma's official terms page.

**Content and License**: When you submit content to Figma (e.g., design files), they use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems (e.g., **Make Designs**, **Visual Search**). Figma does this subject to your settings and applicable law.

**Data Collection and Privacy**: Figma's Privacy Policy explains how they collect and process personal data. This is a separate policy that you should read to understand what data they collect and how it's used.

**Dispute Resolution**: Most users are required to **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)**, which includes **class-action waivers**. This means you can't join a lawsuit with others who have similar claims against Figma. However, new accounts have a **30-day opt-out window**, allowing you to choose a different dispute resolution method.

**Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement, but the terms outline the conditions for this.

The Terms of Service also include:

* A **summary of changes** explaining the key differences between the 2024 and 2023 versions
* Contact information for questions about the terms
* A notice about the previous version of the terms, which is archived for reference
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FIGMA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Figma and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Figma AI features (Make Designs, Visual Search) provisions, clarified that customer file content is not used to train third-party generative models without opt-in, and updated security and incident-notification language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Figma to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.figma.com/legal/tos/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.figma.com/tos/ .

[EXPECTED SUMMARY POINTS]

- Key change: 2024 update added Figma AI features (Make Designs, Visual Search) provisions, clarified that customer file content is not used to train third-party generative models without opt-in, and updated security and incident-notification language.

response:
**Service Name:** Stack Overflow Public Network Terms of Service

Stack Overflow's Terms of Service apply to users who interact with their products and services, as listed on their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** You grant Stack Overflow a license to use your user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems. Be aware that you agree to licensing your Q&A under CC BY-SA (a Creative Commons license). However, there's a restriction on bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement.
* **Privacy:** The Terms don't detail how your personal data is collected, but it cross-references the company's Privacy Policy.
* **Dispute Resolution:** The Terms require you to go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of a court hearing) with class-action waivers. However, you have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either you or Stack Overflow can terminate the agreement, subject to conditions in the live document.

**Potential Concerns for Users:**

* The Terms require you to license your Q&A under CC BY-SA, but impose restrictions on how others can use it.
* You may have limited choices for resolving disputes outside of binding arbitration.
* There's a lack of detail on how Stack Overflow processes personal data.
* Either party can terminate the agreement without notice, although the exact conditions aren't specified.

While the Terms outline key aspects of using Stack Overflow's services, some provisions might be worth closely examining, especially the dispute resolution and content licensing sections.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STACK OVERFLOW PUBLIC NETWORK TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Stack Overflow and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: May 2024 update added a 'Generative AI / LLM' restriction explicitly licensing posted Q&A under CC BY-SA but limiting bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, after the company's content-licensing deals with OpenAI and Google.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Stack Overflow to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public .

**The Quora Terms of Service**

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Quora, a website and platform for asking and answering questions. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope**: These terms apply to Quora's products and services, as described on Quora's official terms page.

**Content and Use**: When you submit content to Quora, we may use it to operate, improve, and train our AI/ML systems. We'll only use your content in accordance with your settings and applicable law.

**Privacy**: Quora's published Privacy Policy describes the types of personal data we collect and how it's processed. We cross-reference this policy in these terms.

**Dispute Resolution**: If a dispute arises, most provisions require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). This means that you can't participate in a class-action lawsuit with others who have similar disputes with Quora. However, this provision applies for only 30 days after opening a new account.

**Termination**: Either you or Quora can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the terms.

**Contact**: If you have questions about these terms, you can find Quora's published legal contact information at [https://www.quora.com/about/tos](https://www.quora.com/about/tos).

**What to Watch Out For**:

* **Arbitration**: This requirement could limit your ability to bring a class-action lawsuit with others who have similar disputes with Quora. This may be a concern if you believe you've been unfairly treated by Quora.
* **Termination**: If Quora or you terminate the agreement, it may affect your use of Quora's products and services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — QUORA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Quora and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Poe (Quora's AI chatbot platform): user prompts/responses may be used to improve Poe and partner models subject to settings, added bot-developer terms, and revised dispute resolution.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Quora to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.quora.com/about/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.quora.com/about/tos .

**Service Name:** The 23andMe Terms of Service

The 23andMe Terms of Service outline the agreement between you and the company when using their products and services. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope:** These terms apply to the products and services listed on the official 23andMe terms page.

**Usage of User Content:** 23andMe uses user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, but only according to your settings and applicable law.

**Privacy:** The terms reference 23andMe's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data they collect and how it's processed.

**Dispute Resolution:** Most users will be required to resolve disputes through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), which has a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. However, users who don't take action within this window will be bound by this agreement.

**Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement according to the live document.

**Notes on Harmful Clauses:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration:** 23andMe requires users to resolve disputes through binding arbitration, which can limit users' ability to take their case to court. If you don't opt out within 30 days of creating an account, you'll be bound by this agreement.
* **Class-Action Waiver:** The terms also limit users' right to participate in class-action lawsuits.
* **Shortened Dispute-Notice Window:** The dispute-notice window was shortened, which may make it more difficult for users to resolve issues.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

The main Terms of Service document is for Twitch. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope**: These terms apply to the products and services on Twitch's official terms page, which likely includes live streaming, video hosting, and other online services.

**Content and License**: When you upload content to Twitch, you're granting them the right to use it to operate and improve their services, including training their AI/ML systems. However, they'll do it based on your settings and the applicable law.

**Privacy**: The Terms of Service don't describe what data Twitch collects or how they process it. Instead, they cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which outlines the categories of personal data and how it's processed.

**Dispute Resolution**: Most users are required to use binding arbitration, which is a private dispute process instead of going to court. This means you won't have the option to take your dispute to a public court. Additionally, you'll need to sign away your right to a class-action lawsuit, where many people with similar grievances can sue together. You can opt out of arbitration within 30 days of creating your account.

**Termination**: Either you or Twitch can terminate the agreement, but there are no specific conditions or notice requirements listed.

**Contact**: For any questions about these Terms of Service, you can find the contact information at the official Twitch website.

**Clauses that may be considered harmful to the user**:

* The binding arbitration requirement and class-action waiver might be unfavorable for users, as they limit your ability to take disputes to a public court and participate in a class-action lawsuit.
* The terms don't offer clear conditions or notice requirements for termination, which could leave you uncertain about when or why the service might be taken away.
* While the Terms of Service link to the company's published Privacy Policy, the policy itself isn't described or embedded in the document, which might lead to uncertainty about what data is being collected and how it's being used.

Keep in mind that these are general observations and not specific legal advice. If you're concerned about the implications of these terms, consider reading the Privacy Policy and understanding how it interacts with these Terms of Service.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TWITCH TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Twitch and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added new Branded Content disclosure rules, expanded the User Content license to support clips, replays and AI-generated highlights, and updated the dispute-resolution mass-arbitration procedure.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Twitch to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ .

**Roblox Terms of Use**

Roblox Terms of Service (TOS) govern your relationship with the platform. The latest version (2024) applies to various Roblox products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

### What They Mean

* **Content and License**: You retain ownership of your submitted content, but Roblox gets permission to use it for their AI/ML systems (if you've allowed it).
* **Privacy**: Your personal data is processed according to the Privacy Policy. We don't disclose more information about data collection here.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). There's a 30-day option to opt out for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can cancel the agreement with conditions described in the live document (which we can't see here).

### Flagged Clauses

* **Dispute Resolution**: Binding arbitration with a class-action waiver might restrict your right to join group lawsuits.
* **Termination**: Conditions are not specified here, but it may be concerning if you're uncertain about what led to termination.

### Important URLs

If you need help or have questions, see the help documentation at [https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us).

### Notable Exceptions

Steam (Valve) has removed mandatory arbitration in their platform; Roblox's policy differs from theirs on this point.

The Terms of Service do not address concerns unrelated to these provisions.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ROBLOX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Roblox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update strengthened minor-protection language (default-private accounts under 13, parental-consent flows), updated Robux/DevEx provisions, added rules for Roblox's generative-AI 'Studio Assistant' and avatar-creation tools, and revised arbitration class-waiver section.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Roblox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 .

**Service Name:** Steam Subscriber Agreement

The Steam Subscriber Agreement governs your relationship with Steam (Valve) when using their products and services. Here's a plain-language summary of the key provisions:

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope**: These terms apply to your use of Steam products and services, as listed on their official terms page.
2. **Content and License**: Steam uses your submitted content to improve and train their AI/ML systems, but only according to your settings and applicable law.
3. **Privacy**: Your personal data is governed by Steam's separate Privacy Policy.
4. **Dispute Resolution**: Most terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers, but you can opt out within 30 days of account creation.
5. **Termination**: Either party can end the agreement under specific conditions.

**Potentially Harmful Clauses:**

* The mandatory arbitration (dispute resolution) clause, which may limit your ability to seek justice in court. However, it's worth noting that Steam is the only notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024.
* The class-action waiver, which prohibits you from participating in group lawsuits against Steam.

**Other Notes:**

* Steam reserves the right to terminate the agreement under specific conditions.
* For questions or concerns, you can contact Steam through their published legal contact information on the Steam Subscriber Agreement webpage.
* The previous version of the terms is available through the Internet Archive (https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/).

Please keep in mind that these terms are subject to change, and it's always a good idea to review the latest version to ensure you're comfortable with the agreement.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STEAM SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Steam (Valve) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: September 26, 2024 update removed the mandatory arbitration / class-action waiver clauses entirely - Valve now requires disputes to be filed in court (subject to venue rules), reversing several years of arbitration-only language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Steam (Valve) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ .

5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos .

**Service Name:** DoorDash Consumer Terms of Service

The Terms of Service govern your relationship with DoorDash, which provides various products and services for food delivery, as described on their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to the services you use on DoorDash.
* **Content and License:** DoorDash can use your user-submitted content, including text and data, to improve their systems, but this is subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The terms reference DoorDash's published Privacy Policy, which outlines what data they collect and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes must be resolved through **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to certain conditions.

**Potential Concerns for Users:**

* **Arbitration Clause:** Requiring disputes to be resolved through binding arbitration means that users won't have the option to take the issue to court, which could limit access to important consumer protections.
* **Data Usage:** DoorDash can use your content to improve their systems without clear limitations or oversight, which raises questions about data protection and control.
* **Termination:** The terms don't specify the exact conditions for termination, which could leave users unsure about when or why their account might be closed.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DOORDASH CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with DoorDash and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised arbitration provisions (including mass-arbitration handling), added DashPass auto-renewal clarifications, updated tipping/refund mechanics and added new sections covering AI-generated menu summaries and order-suggestion features.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by DoorDash to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service .

**Service Name:** Uber US Terms of Use

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope:** These terms apply to Uber's products and services as described on the official terms page.
2. **Content License:** Uber uses user-submitted content to improve and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. (This means Uber can use information you provide to improve its services, but only in ways you've agreed to.)
3. **Privacy:** Uber's published Privacy Policy explains how personal data is collected and processed. (You can find the full policy by contacting the company.)
4. **Dispute Resolution:** You agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a class-action waiver. However, there's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. (This means you'll likely resolve disputes outside of court, without joining a class action lawsuit.)
5. **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement with notice.
6. **Contact:** For questions, see the company's published contact information.

**Harmful Clauses to Note:**

* **Dispute Resolution:** The requirement for binding arbitration with a class-action waiver may limit your ability to take part in class action lawsuits, which can be beneficial for collective action.
* **Content License:** While Uber can use user-submitted content for improvement, it's unclear how this affects data protection or potential biases in AI algorithms.
* **Termination:** Without stating specific grounds, either party can terminate the agreement, which might leave users without notice or recourse.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — UBER US TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Uber and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised arbitration after the New Jersey Uber Eats arbitration decision, added language on AI-generated trip summaries and driver/rider safety features, and expanded liability sections regarding third-party services.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Uber to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.uber.com/legal/en/document/?country=united-states&lang=en&name=general-terms-of-use . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.uber.com/legal/en/document/?country=united-states&lang=en&name=general-terms-of-use .

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope:** These Terms of Service apply to Airbnb's products and services, including any new features or services added in the future.
2. **Content and License:** When you use Airbnb, you're giving the company permission to use your submitted content (like photos, reviews, and ratings) to run its business, improve its services, and train its AI systems.

However, there's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, allowing you to opt out of arbitration and have your disputes resolved in court.
5. **Termination:** Either you or Airbnb can end the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the live document. (Unfortunately, the document doesn't provide clear information on these conditions.)

**Harmful Clauses to the User:**

* The Terms of Service require binding arbitration with a class-action waiver, which might limit your ability to seek justice through the court system.
* You waive your right to join (or become part of) a group lawsuit against Airbnb.
* If you have concerns about your relationship with Airbnb, you should carefully review the arbitration provision and consider opting out within the 30-day window (if applicable).

**Contact Information:** For questions or concerns about these Terms of Service, you can visit Airbnb's Help Center at [https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2908](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2908).

Please keep in mind that these Terms of Service may change over time. Always review them before using Airbnb's services.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — AIRBNB TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Airbnb and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added new AnyWhere/Icons experience terms, revised cancellation and refund policies (including AirCover updates), added language on automated/AI-driven listing detection (e.g. anti-party tools), and updated arbitration provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Airbnb to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2908 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2908 .
